record.original_question: Which spectral types can occur for ergodic measure-preserving automorphisms? In particular, does there exist an ergodic automorphism with absolutely continuous spectrum that is not Lebesgue, and which sets of spectral multiplicities can be realized by ergodic automorphisms?

evidence.quote: Q3. Какими спектрами могут обладать эргодические автоморфизмы? Существует ли автоморфизм с абсолютно непрерывным нелебеговским спектром? Какие наборы спектральных кратностей могут быть у эргодического автоморфизма?
Неизвестно, имеются ли эргодические автоморфизмы вероятностного пространства, у которых наборы спектральных кратностей имеют, например, вид {m, m + 1}, m > 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ be a standard non-atomic Lebesgue probability space, and let $T:X\to X$ be an invertible measure-preserving transformation (an automorphism). Recall that $T$ is ergodic if every $T$-invariant measurable set has measure $0$ or $1$. Associated with $T$ is the Koopman unitary operator $U_T$ acting on $L^2_0(X,\mu)=\{f\in L^2(X,\mu):\int f\,d\mu=0\}$ by $U_T f=f\circ T$. By the spectral theorem for unitary operators, $U_T$ is determined up to unitary equivalence by its maximal spectral type (an equivalence class of finite Borel measures on the unit circle $S^1$) and its multiplicity function $m_T:S^1\to\{1,2,\dots\}\cup\{\infty\}$, defined up to a set of measure zero with respect to the maximal spectral type. The set of essential values of $m_T$ is called the set of spectral multiplicities of $T$.

Address the following three questions:

(a) Characterize which spectral types (i.e., which equivalence classes of finite Borel measures on $S^1$, together with admissible multiplicity functions) can be realized as the spectral data of some ergodic automorphism of $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$.

(b) Does there exist an ergodic automorphism $T$ whose maximal spectral type is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure on $S^1$, but is not equivalent to Lebesgue measure itself?

(c) Determine which subsets $E\subseteq\{1,2,3,\dots\}\cup\{\infty\}$ can occur as the set of spectral multiplicities of an ergodic automorphism. In particular, for an integer $m>2$, can the two-element set $\{m,\,m+1\}$ be realized as the set of spectral multiplicities of some ergodic automorphism?
artifact.status_search_result: The general realization problem for spectral types and spectral multiplicity sets of ergodic measure-preserving automorphisms is a classical open problem in the spectral theory of dynamical systems. While many specific multiplicity sets have been realized (e.g., sets containing 1 or 2 are realizable by mixing transformations, and many finite sets including 2 are realizable by weakly mixing automorphisms), the general question—and the specific case of realizing sets of the form $\{m,m+1\}$ for $m>2$—remains open according to recent surveys.

status_evidence.title: A survey on spectral multiplicities of ergodic actions (Danilenko)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey describing the spectral multiplicity problem as a weak version of a main open problem in spectral theory of dynamical systems, listing many realizable sets but leaving the general characterization open.
status_evidence.claim: The realization problem for spectral multiplicity sets of ergodic transformations is open in general.

status_evidence.title: Spectral theory of dynamical systems (Kanigowski–Lemańczyk)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing open problems on spectral types and multiplicities for ergodic automorphisms.
status_evidence.claim: Characterization of realizable spectral types and multiplicity sets remains an open research direction.
